value: Public domain (U.S. federal government report; U.S. DOE Industrial Technologies Program). No reuse terms printed.

BCS, Incorporated (2007). Mining Industry Energy Bandwidth Study. Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy, Industrial Technologies Program (Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy), Washington, DC. June 2007. No report number or DOI printed.

CURRENT -> variant efficiency-base; BEST PRACTICE -> bat; PRACTICAL MINIMUM -> efficiency-strong (same convention as the 2015-2017 DOE bandwidth extractions, but a SINGLE printed practical-minimum value goes in value with no max). THEORETICAL minimum is a physical floor and is in _other-values.

Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 4). Loaded: Exhibits 23-25 (Appendix B), equipment-level energy requirements in Btu/ton for coal, metal and industrial-mineral mining, neglecting electricity losses (onsite energy), converted to kWh/t (electric equipment) or GJ/t (diesel or mixed) per tonne. Exhibit 26 (TBtu/yr including 3.17x electricity losses) is not loaded; the methodology (Sect. 4.3) is in other-values. Carrier: stated only where the equipment is clearly electric (fans, pumps, conveyor motors, LHD) or diesel; drilling, blasting, digging and ancillary are mixed (target total); crushing, grinding, flotation, centrifuge and separations are treated as electricity (inferred: Appendix D gives electric motor efficiencies; DOE 2002 Table 7-3 lists the mills as electric) - the coordinator should confirm. Traps: (1) Btu/ton is per ton of MATERIAL HANDLED (Sect. 4), so per-ton values for processing look per ton of ore processed while haulage values are per ton of all material (ore plus waste) - bases are mixed and a metal-mining whole-industry total in Exhibit 14 (342,200 Btu/ton of material mined, with losses) is NOT the sum of Exhibit 24 (168,746, no losses). (2) Printed short tons; converted with 0.907185 t/short ton. (3) Mineral crushing current is blank in the table; derived as crush-and-grind 2,700 minus grind 300. (4) Mineral separations current 1,300 vs best practice 100 is a printed 13x drop and flotation is only 100 - treat with care; Separations is an aggregate row that includes centrifuge and flotation, so do not add them. (5) Practical-minimum values are modelled (mostly the 2/3 rule), not measured, and the model mines are US SHERPA hypothetical mines (SAG/ball milling for gold), not Canadian. (6) Coal electric-equipment practical efficiency prints 0%; the table is pre-aggregated, so the Electric Equipment subtotal rows and the Crushing-and-Grinding aggregate rows are not loaded. No costs, no TRL.
